title: Proactive buffering for KEDA trigger spikes causing cold-start cascades
creator: Ava Chen
description: Postmortem and action plan for an incident where transient KEDA trigger spikes caused repeated cold-start cascades in the inference serving fleet. The incident exposed a sensitivity mismatch between KEDA scaledObject triggers (percentile-derived metrics) and the runtime's cold-start behaviour; noisy percentile sampling produced scale decisions that over-indexed on short-lived spikes and drained warm capacity during a rolling upgrade.
incident_summary: 2026-02-26 14:05 UTC: Increased tail latency observed in hosted-api region eu-west-1; Grafana alert: 'inference.request_queue_age.p90 > 250ms'
14:07 UTC: KEDA scaler reacted to short-lived percentile spikes, issuing scale-up to new pods and concurrently triggering scale-down of idle warm-pool instances due to an unrelated autoscaler policy
14:09—14:20 UTC: Repeated cold-starts (KV cache misses) amplified latency and CPU, producing more percentile spikes (feedback loop).
14:35 UTC: Customer-facing error rate for high-concurrency routes increased to 3.8% (baseline 0.1%); SRE paging engaged and mitigation runbook executed.
15:00 UTC: Emergency mitigation applied — override KEDA trigger to median-based metric and paused scheduled scale-downs; latency recovered to baseline by 15:12 UTC.
timeline: 2026-02-26 13:50 UTC — rolling canary job started for runtime-1.22 on eu-west-1 pool
14:05 UTC — spike in request_queue_age.p90 reported; coincident low warm-pool headroom due to canary reservations
14:07 UTC — KEDA scaledObject triggered 2x scale-up; HPA stabilization window clashed with KEDA cooldown settings
14:10 UTC — warm instances started being reclaimed by scheduled scale-down job (bug: missing grace window), resulting in net capacity loss
14:25 UTC — SRE applied median-based override and increased HPA minReplicas for impacted pool
15:12 UTC — metrics stable and incident declared mitigated; postmortem investigation started
root_cause: A confluence of three issues: (1) KEDA configured to use p90 of a sampled histogram (request_queue_age.p90) which is noisy on short windows; (2) a scheduled warm-pool scale-down job ran without observing ongoing scale decisions (missing grace window), and (3) HPA/KEDA cooldown and stabilization windows were misaligned causing oscillation. Together these caused positive feedback where cold starts produced percentile spikes which in turn triggered more cold starts.
impact: Short-duration capacity outages in eu-west-1 for ~67 minutes total (from anomaly to full recovery). Customer-facing error rate peaked at 3.8% on high-concurrency endpoints; internal SLO blips recorded: 99.5th latency moved from 210ms to 860ms during peak. No data loss; no security impact.
mitigation: Emergency: switched KEDA trigger from request_queue_age.p90 to request_queue_age.p50 (median) for eu-west-1 pool
Paused all scheduled warm-pool scale-down jobs until grace-window fix deployed
Raised HPA minReplicas for impacted pool by +2 for 24 hours
Follow-up: open PR to add metric smoothing and debounce logic in KEDA scaler plugin (see links)
Added an incident note and updated runbook with new decision tree for percentile spikes
root_cause_analysis_notes: Percentile metrics (p90) were computed from a Prometheus histogram that has coarse bucketization for short-lived workloads; when traffic is bursty, p90 becomes sensitive to single outlier samples.
KEDA's scaler executes at a 30s sampling cadence; combined with a 60s HPA stabilizationWindow and a 45s scheduled warm-pool drain, the timings produced opportunities for oscillation.
The rolling canary consumed headroom in the warm pool due to reservation configuration, reducing buffer available to absorb a transient spike.
action_items: A1: Implement percentile smoothing in KEDA scaler plugin: exponentially weighted smoothing across last 5 samples to reduce sensitivity to single-sample outliers. Owner: Diego Martinez. ETA: 2026-03-19. Tracking: GH PR #5872.

A2: Add a proactive warm-pool 'buffer' feature: keep a small, predictive pool that grows briefly based on smoothed slope of request_queue_age.p50/p90. Owner: Priya Rao. ETA: 2026-03-26. Design doc: Confluence 'Warm-pool buffer strategy' (link below).

A3: Fix scheduled warm-pool drain to respect active scaler decisions and add a configurable grace window (default 10min). Owner: SRE team (Jamal Reed). ETA: 2026-03-12. Patch deployed 2026-03-10 to prevent immediate re-occurrence.
A4: Align KEDA scaler cadence, HPA stabilizationWindow, and warm-pool drain timing; introduce a policy validator to surface unsafe combos in CI. Owner: Platform Core (Nina Patel). ETA: 2026-04-02.
A5: Add synthetic load tests that reproduce percentile spike to CI gating for autoscaler changes. Owner: QE (Marco Silva). ETA: 2026-03-30.
A6: Update runbook and dashboard to include 'percentile spike checklist' and automated mitigation toggle. Owner: SRE runbooks (Ava Chen). ETA: 2026-03-08. Runbook updated 2026-03-03.
A7: Post-deploy monitoring: add a dedicated Grafana panel with smoothed p50/p90 and a derived 'spike_energy' signal to alert before oscillation. Owner: Observability (Lina Qureshi). ETA: 2026-03-22.
decisions: Switch default KEDA scaler metric from p90 to p50 for bursty routes until smoothing is implemented (accepted).
Prioritize 'proactive warm-pool buffer' feature as a short-term mitigation instead of enlarging global minReplicas (accepted).
Require any autoscaler / warm-pool change to include a synthetic spike test in CI (accepted).
Do not increase cost-sensitive global reserved capacity; prefer smarter buffering and smoothing.
comments: 2026-03-03 — Ava Chen: Warm-pool drain grace-window patch deployed to production (eu-west-1). Short-term mitigation reduced recurrence risk.
2026-03-05 — Diego Martinez: Initial smoothing prototype in branch 'keda-smooth' shows reduced oscillation in canary test (results attached to PR #5872).
2026-03-09 — SRE (Jamal Reed): Verified runbook updates and added emergency toggle to Pause KEDA scaler for a single pool. Test drill scheduled 2026-03-16.
2026-03-12 — PM review (Sofia Li): Approved prioritization for buffer feature; requested cost estimate for 6-month horizon.
